title: The owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“Formation-counting amounts are live at resolution”) counts 'my formation' by OWNER, not by control
summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“Formation-counting amounts are live at resolution”) words Embermaw Fledgling's X ('the number of attacking units in my formation') as the surviving units its controller OWNS in the battle columns. A unit its controller controls but does not own (raised from the enemy bin by Wake the Dead, or lent by Uglk; the owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“Cosmic Reversal reaches the board; every…”) makes such units ordinary allies) attacks in the same formation and should be counted. If the engine counts by owner, it undercounts. Suspected from the ruling's wording only; a probe should attack with a borrowed unit beside Embermaw Fledgling and read X.

evidence.quote: units the controller owns in `battle.columns` at trigger resolution

closed: the engine counts by control (Embermaw Fledgling reads u.controller === self.controller), so nothing undercounts; what stands is the ruling text saying "owns", filed with the stale register text.

title: Throwing Boulder's 'adjacent enemy' test cannot show what its title claims
summary: 18-earth-c 'the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“"Activate this ability only if …"…”): an ALLY is required — an adjacent enemy does not unlock it' sets up the enemy as a blocker facing the Boulder. Under the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“Joining a formation is a CHOICE…”) adjacency (the three positions inside the unit's own formation) a facing blocker is not adjacent at all, so the Boulder has no adjacent unit of any kind and the test passes whether or not the gate checks that the neighbour is an ALLY. Either the test is vacuous, or the engine treats the facing enemy as adjacent, which the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“Joining a formation is a CHOICE…”) does not allow. A real guard needs an enemy unit inside the Boulder's own formation, for example a unit stolen into it, or a probe of the adjacency query with a facing blocker.

evidence.quote: CR 111.7b: an ALLY is required — an enemy blocking it (facing, not adjacent) does not unlock it

closed: fixed on 2026-10-24 (CT-241): narrowed to what the board can build, an enemy facing it, not adjacent.

title: Defending formation adjacency ignores unblocked columns between blockers
summary: adjacentInFormation builds the defender grid from the sorted block keys, so blockers on attacking columns 1 and 3 (column 2 unblocked) are treated as left/right neighbours. Inspiration then buffs across the gap (round-1 verifier probe on combat.columns.adjacency). The Manual makes blocking position matter for adjacency, and a blocking column is keyed to the attacking column it faces, so the unblocked column is a gap. The engine's own comment calls its reading an approximation. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

evidence.quote: is set, the units are locked in position and are considered
CR 606.1f / CT-249: blockers either side of an unblocked column are not adjacent, so Inspiration does not buff across the gap

closed: fixed on 2026-10-22 (CT-249): the defending grid keeps an unblocked attacking column as a gap, so blockers either side of it are not neighbours (560).

title: A lone Hooba-Lin killed under its attack trigger makes its 1/1 outside the formation
summary: Hooba-Lin attacks alone and is killed with its attack trigger on the stack, before blocks. Its column collapses away, the attacker is offered no position, and the 1/1 is created outside any formation. The designer's [Solved] answer names Hooba-Lin among the effects that 'will remember they were in formation and will work fine', with no exception for a lone attacker; rule 602.6f states that and 602.6k excepts it. The engine applies the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“Joining a formation is a CHOICE…”)’s 'no living unit, no slots' instead. It may be an unruled edge rather than a bug (D-U10-6). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

closed: fixed on 2026-10-22 (CT-250): a dead source places into the formation it remembers even when that formation is empty (561, Hooba-Lin, -Bot, -God and -Pon).

title: A source that left play places nothing when its remembered formation is now empty
summary: The owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“An effect whose source has left…”)/RAQ: Hooba-Lin killed with its attack trigger on the stack "will remember [it was] in formation and will work fine". With a lone Hooba-Lin attacking, formationSeatOf returns its last-known seat but formationSlots returns no slot for a grid with no living unit, so the 1/1 is created outside the formation ("no open position in the formation"). Applies to every the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“Joining a formation is a CHOICE…”) placer reading a dead source (Hooba-Bot, Hooba-Pon, Hooba-Lin).

title: Stack-effect targets are not region-filtered
summary: pushStackTargets offers every item on the single game stack as a 'target effect'/'target spell effect' with no check of the item's region against the resolving region, contrary to 'every single effect is specific to the region it takes place in'. Already tracked as F-U01-2; probe shows an item stamped with another region is offered in battle. Natural reachability not demonstrated.
